subject: Re: Proposal to switch Storify billing to prepaid yearly commitment
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena@storify.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2025-11-18T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Inquiry: moving Storify to prepaid annual commitment

Hi Rishi,

We're looking at consolidating our inference spend and would like to explore switching Storify from monthly billing to an annual prepay commitment for 2026. Current ask from our finance team: can you provide a simple proposal that shows: term discount tiers (1yr vs 2yr), how a ramp schedule would be handled if we grow usage mid-year, and payment/invoice cadence options?

High-level numbers: estimated monthly spend today $8k–12k (spiky). We expect 2–3x growth in first year. Important: procurement wants simple, predictable invoicing and a clause for unused committed capacity (prefer credits vs refunds). Also need confirmation on SOC 2 and basic data segregation language.

Can you put together a short proposal and an example ramp schedule?

Thanks,
Elena
Director of Platform Partnerships
Storify.ai

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: Elena Torres <elena@storify.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: 2025-11-19T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Inquiry: moving Storify to prepaid annual commitment

Thanks for the clear brief, Elena — appreciate the details. Quick summary of what we can offer and what I'll attach as a concise proposal: 

- Pricing: baseline (current month-to-month) will be represented as our list hosted price for your usage profile. For a 12‑month prepaid commitment we can offer a 30% effective discount off your current blended rate. For a 24‑month commit we can add an additional 5% (35% total) provided the annual minimum is met.
- Ramp schedule: we propose a quarterly ramp buffer: you prepay for an annual committed volume, and if usage in any quarter exceeds the committed quarterly allocation we bill overage at the committed discounted rate. If actual annual usage is below committed volume at year-end, we propose converting the shortfall into platform credits usable for the following 6 months. Refunds are only available for extraordinary cases (rare).
- Invoice cadence: single upfront invoice (preferred) or two invoices (50/50) permitted. We can do net 45/60 payment terms for enterprise customers with a valid PO.
- Protections: 6‑week price protection window from signature for any published list-price movement; SOC2 attestation and data segregation language included in the SOW.

I'll attach a short proposal + a sample ramp schedule and the SOW. If procurement wants DocuSign, we can send that link.

I'll note this is an approval request for a 30% discount standard play; anything beyond that (deeper concession or credit structure changes) will need finance sign-off. Looping Marissa and Jordan for visibility.

Next steps: I'll send the proposal and ramp example formally; happy to jump on a 30-min cadence call with procurement next week if that helps.

Best,
Rishi
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: 2025-11-20T08:45:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Inquiry: moving Storify to prepaid annual commitment

Rishi — thanks for the draft. A few internal notes from finance/ops: 

- 30% for 1yr / 35% for 2yr is within our band for this ARR level, but we need to lock the credit conversion mechanics: convert unused committed spend into account credits that expire 6 months after contract anniversary. No cash refunds.
- Approve net 45 for first invoice; require PO before we issue invoice.
- If they want a split invoice (50/50) we tie the second invoice to a milestone (start of Q3) to reduce credit exposure.
- For ramp protection, offer a 10% buffer per quarter (so committed quarterly allocation = annual_commit/4 + 10% floor). Overages billed monthly at discounted rate.

If Storify pushes for refunds or longer credit windows, escalate to sales leadership. Jordan, can you prepare a final pricing sheet and the ramp table with formulas (committed annual volume -> quarterly allocation + buffer)?

-Marissa
Head of Finance, Commercial
Redwood Inference

From: Elena Torres <elena@storify.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@storify.ai
Date: 2025-12-02T13:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Proposal to switch Storify billing to prepaid yearly commitment

Rishi — thanks for the outline. Procurement had two follow-ups before we can move to signatures: 

1) They want to see the exact invoice schedule language and an example invoice (we need line items for prepaid, reserved capacity, overage rates, and credits).
2) They asked whether Redwood will accept a single annual invoice issued on signature with net 60 payment terms (Storify prefers 60). If not, they want a 50/50 split with the second invoice issued at month 7.

Also: please confirm SOC2 date (we need attestation dated within last 12 months) and include the data segregation sentence for the SOW: "Customer data will be logically segmented and customer-specific keys will be used for encryption at rest."

Procurement would also like DocuSign on the final SOW and a link to the pricing sheet in HubSpot.

We'll review as soon as you send the doc.

Best,
Elena

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: Elena Torres <elena@storify.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: 2026-01-05T16:55:00-08:00
Subject: Final proposal and DocuSign: Storify prepaid commitment (12 months)

Elena — attaching the formal proposal and SOW per procurement's asks. Highlights: 

- Offer: 12‑month prepaid commitment for $120,000 billed upfront (single invoice) with net 60 terms (approved per Marissa for Storify). This represents an effective 30% discount vs your current blended monthly pricing at current run-rate.
- Overages: monthly overage invoiced at the committed discounted rate.
- Credits: annual shortfalls convert to platform credits valid for 6 months post-anniversary.
- Ramp mechanics: committed annual volume is split into quarters; each quarter carries a 10% buffer. Any quarter-to-quarter surge beyond buffer is billed as overage. Example schedule attached in the pricing sheet.
- SOC2: latest attestation dated 2025-06-10 included; SOW includes the requested data segregation sentence.

Attachments: Storify_Proposal_v2.pdf; Redwood_Pricing_Sheet_Q1-2026.xlsx; SOW_Storify_2026.docx

DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.net/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?PowerFormId=abcdef-123456

A couple of concessions we made to close quickly: acceptance of net 60 (finance exception) and conversion-to-credits (no refunds). This is conditioned on signing the SOW with the attached pricing sheet.

If this looks good, execute via the DocuSign link and we'll provision the reserved capacity in our Dedicated pool and schedule the onboarding kickoff.

Thanks,
Rishi

From: Elena Torres <elena@storify.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@storify.ai
Date: 2026-01-05T17:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Final proposal and DocuSign: Storify prepaid commitment (12 months)

Rishi — received, thank you. I'll run this through procurement today and aim to return a signed DocuSign by next week. Procurement noted the net 60 and the credit approach — they will confirm formally. Also copying in our legal for the SOW review.

Appreciate the fast turnaround.

Elena
